dedupe_keys.name: federal reserve g 17 industrial production and capacity utilization

description: The G.17 statistical release publishes monthly indexes of US industrial production and the related measures of capacity and capacity utilisation for manufacturing, mining and electric and gas utilities, by NAICS industry and market group. It is produced by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Coverage is national with industry detail, and utilisation series run from 1972; each release revises recent months and an annual revision, usually in November, benchmarks the indexes to census and agency data. Data are available as HTML and PDF tables, ASCII and XML files, the Fed's Data Download Program and FRED at the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; access is free, as public US Government statistics. Caveats: the release notes that the Data Download Program faces eventual retirement in favour of FRED, and capacity estimates rest on annual benchmark data that arrive with a lag, so recent months are provisional. For simulation it supports capacity planning and resilience analysis, for example measuring the output drop and recovery of industries after hurricanes or supply shocks and calibrating the spare capacity assumed in cascading failure models of production networks. It complements the US Census Annual Survey of Manufactures record, which gives establishment-based annual detail for the same industries.
